one-check-per-line.why: all 2 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 2

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "node bin/csv2json.js --tsv reads tab-separated input on stdin and prints the sam"

words-only.why: Check 2 is fine. "Documents --tsv" reasonably requires README.md to mention the flag and say what it does. Check 1 is stricter than its expect line. That line only requires the --tsv output to match whatever `node bin/csv2json.js` prints for the same table as CSV, and the `cmp` step already tests that. But PASS also requires the output to be "a JSON array of objects keyed by the header row", namely the exact array "[{"name":"Ann","age":"30","city":"Oslo"},...]". FAIL includes "the --tsv output is not that JSON array". That pins the CSV path's own output to a fixed value, which is a regression check on CSV behaviour that the words don't require. If a pull request changed CSV output and the TSV output still matched it, the check would wrongly fail. The brief already lists "plain CSV output … is unchanged" under Advisory, so this fixed-value check belongs there too, not in PASS/FAIL.

runs-as-written.why: I went through every command in both briefs against the 6 tracked files and package.json. `npm test` maps to the `node --test` script, which finds test/csv.test.js. `node bin/csv2json.js` and `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv` use a script that exists, and the builder adds the flag before the verifier runs it. `parse(input, '\t')` fits the stated `parse(text, sep = ',')` signature. In the verifier, the `printf '...\t...\n' | node ... > /tmp/x; echo "exit $?"` lines are valid shell, and `$?` holds node's exit status. `cmp /tmp/tsv.out /tmp/csv.out && cat` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` are valid; the `--` stops grep reading the pattern as an option. The one borderline case is `node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`, which needs a file that doesn't exist. But it is only an example line to put in README.md, not a command the brief tells anyone to run. Step 5's "run both commands by hand" is plain prose. No command breaks.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and all are handled. Item 1: the builder brief says "Plain CSV behaviour must not change at all" and "Run `npm test` and make sure every test passes", though no expect line asks for either. Item 2: the verifier brief has an "Advisory (not pass/fail)" section that says to run `npm test` and check that plain CSV output is unchanged. Neither appears in any PASS or FAIL condition. It never says outright that no expect line covers them, but the "not pass/fail" label makes clear they are advice, which is what this item is after. Item 3: Check 1 feeds the same table as TSV with --tsv and as CSV without the flag, then compares the two outputs with `cmp`, for two different tables.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked the verifier brief against both must_not items. It has exactly two checks, one for each expect line. Check 1 runs the TSV vs CSV comparison, and Check 2 greps and reads README.md. npm test and the plain-CSV regression appear only under "Advisory (not pass/fail)", so they are not counted as checks and cannot change the verdict. That means there is no third check. Check 1's PASS/FAIL conditions cover only exit codes, the cmp result and the JSON shape. Check 2's cover only whether README mentions --tsv and says what it does. Neither one requires npm test or the CSV tests to pass. The builder brief does ask the builder to run npm test, but that is not a verifier PASS/FAIL condition. Neither must_not item is broken.

methods-private.why:
I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief, looking for probes that appear in both. Step 3 of the builder brief gives specific inputs and an expected output: TSV input 'a	b
1	2
', compared against CSV 'a,b
1,2
', which should print '[{"a":"1","b":"2"}]
'. Check 1 of the verifier brief uses the same table as its second case ("Repeat with a second table, a	b / 1	b against a,b / 1,2"). The verifier's advisory also expects the same output, [{"a":"1","b":"2"}]. Step 5 also has the builder confirm the outputs are byte-identical, which matches the verifier's cmp check. Telling the builder to write its own tests is allowed. But putting the verifier's exact inputs and expected output in the builder brief hands it a probe, so the criterion fails.
